metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Does a moderate post-civil-war P1 (pre ~0.488, Tier 2) absorb a sovereign default (2022) and a mass-uprising presidential ouster (the Aragalaya) WITHOUT territorial fragmentation? Mod8 (agency split): mass protest forcing PEACEFUL leadership change rather than state breakup or large-scale violence.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record; single entity (Sri Lanka). 2022 sovereign default (first in its history), Aragalaya protest movement, July 2022 flight/resignation of President Gotabaya Rajapaksa, parliamentary selection of Ranil Wickremesinghe, 2023 IMF Extended Fund Facility. Scored ~2018 vs 2024. GOOD data.

pre_event.event_description: On the eve of the crisis (post-2009 civil-war end, after the 2018 constitutional crisis), Sri Lanka carried a moderate institutional base but accumulating external debt, tax cuts, and foreign-reserve depletion that culminated in the 2022 default and the Aragalaya mass-protest movement.

context.fragmentation_mechanism: economic crisis (sovereign default) without territorial fragmentation

Sri Lanka.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Moderate post-civil-war P1 (pre ~0.488, Tier 2) with strong human-capital pillars (high P3/P4) but a thin economic-cohesion base - the configuration the framework expects to absorb a fiscal shock without breaking up.

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Disruptive-but-contained: a moderate P1 absorbs the default and leadership ouster with an MI dip (likely Tier 2 -> Tier 3) but no institutional collapse or fragmentation; recovery via an IMF program.
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Pre-P1 ~0.488 (Tier 2, moderate) high enough to channel a fiscal shock through institutions; economic pillars take the hit, the state holds.
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Sri Lanka fragments territorially, suffers institutional (not merely economic) collapse, or descends into sustained large-scale violence.

b_violence.prediction: Mass mobilization with limited violence; the Aragalaya forces a PEACEFUL leadership change rather than civil war or breakup (Mod8 agency split).
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY - mass protest channelled into a peaceful transfer
b_violence.falsification_condition: Large-scale lethal civil conflict or violent regime seizure.

c_convergence.prediction: N/A (single entity); self-trajectory: shock then partial recovery.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Failure concentrated in the economic-structure / fiscal pillars (P4 plus economic cohesion), not in core institutional capacity (P1), which holds.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias.
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Failure driven by an institutional (P1) collapse rather than the economic pillars.

f_reversal_risk.prediction: N/A - not a democratic-transition reversal case.

g_suppression_mechanism.classification: N/A - economic crisis, not a suppression case.

Sri Lanka.outcome_summary: Disruptive-but-contained, as predicted. The 2022 default and Aragalaya forced President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee and resign; Parliament selected a successor (Wickremesinghe), an IMF Extended Fund Facility (2023) anchored stabilization, and the 2024 presidential election peacefully elected Anura Kumara Dissanayake - a peaceful leadership turnover, not state breakup. MI dipped 0.607 -> 0.541 (Tier 2 -> Tier 3) with P1 near-flat 0.488 -> 0.452; the shock landed on the economic pillars (P4 0.866 -> 0.604), not on core institutional capacity.
key_events: 2022 first-ever sovereign default; foreign-reserve depletion, fuel/food/medicine shortages
Aragalaya mass protest movement; July 2022 occupation of the presidential residence
President Gotabaya Rajapaksa flees and resigns; Parliament selects Wickremesinghe

a_trajectory.evidence: MI 0.607 -> 0.541 (Tier 2 -> Tier 3); P1 near-flat 0.488 -> 0.452; default + ouster absorbed without fragmentation; IMF program.
a_trajectory.explanation: Moderate P1 channelled a maximal fiscal shock through institutions - disruptive-but-contained, as predicted.

b_violence.evidence: Mass mobilization with limited violence forced a peaceful leadership change (resignation + parliamentary succession + 2024 election), not civil war.
b_violence.explanation: Mod8 agency split realized: protest -> peaceful transfer, as predicted.

analysis.overall_assessment: Clean confirmation: 4/4 applicable predictions CONFIRMED (d PARTIAL under the strict re-code). A moderate P1 absorbed a sovereign default and a presidential ouster without fragmentation, via a peaceful transfer of power.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: A moderate (Tier 2) post-civil-war institutional base can absorb a catastrophic economic shock and an extra-constitutional pressure event and still resolve it CONSTITUTIONALLY: the Aragalaya forced a peaceful leadership change rather than state breakup, with the damage confined to the economic pillars while core institutional capacity held. The economic-crisis counterpart to Argentina (case28) on the South Asian, post-conflict end of the P1 range.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; adds an economic-crisis-without-fragmentation confirmation and a clean Mod8 (protest -> peaceful transfer) instance.
